nodes.description: The c.1965+1dup allele generates intron-16 one-base retention and exon-16 skipping in minigene assays. Carrier-mother blood RNA contains the one-base-retention product alongside normally spliced transcript; exon skipping was not demonstrated in that blood experiment. Altered protein products are predicted consequences, whereas neuronal protein abundance and Mediator assembly were not measured. Arg224Gly did not alter splicing in the tested constructs. A separate 2026 report describes intron-2 retention associated with c.180+5G>C.

evidence.snippet: In vitro MSA results indicated that the variant c.670C > G (p.R224G) did not disrupt the normal splicing of the MED25 gene (Supplementary Figure S3). In contrast, the variant c.1965 + 1dup affected normal splicing, resulting in two abnormal transcripts: retention of 1 bp in intron 16; skipping of exon 16 (Figure 2).

nodes.description: Homozygous variant reported in seven patients from four families in the same Israeli village. Co-immunoprecipitation demonstrates impaired Mediator association; this result should not be generalized to all MED25 missense alleles.

evidence.reference_title: Homozygous MED25 mutation implicated in eye-intellectual disability syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Using exome sequencing, we have been able to identify homozygous mutation p.(Tyr39Cys) in MED25 as the cause of a syndrome characterized by eye, brain, cardiac and palatal abnormalities as well as growth retardation, microcephaly and severe intellectual disability in seven patients from four unrelated families, all originating from the same village.

evidence.reference_title: Homozygous MED25 mutation implicated in eye-intellectual disability syndrome.
evidence.snippet: The MED25 point mutation is located in the von Willebrand factor type A (MED25 VWA) domain which is responsible for MED25 recruitment into the Mediator complex; co-immunoprecipitation experiment demonstrated that this mutation dramatically impairs MED25 interaction with the Mediator complex in mammalian cells.
